gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a combo 'adapter + converter' only steps the voltage down on its marked converter outlets. TESSAN's own page for its combo says the '200W adapter area' is only 'suitable for electrical appliances with voltages of 100V-240V', so plugging a 110V-only device into the wrong socket of the same unit gives it full wall voltage. TESSAN's TC03 page lists only phones, tablets, cameras, headphones and small personal electronics as its use, with a 250 W ceiling.
standout_why: Rivals I opened: plugvoltage.com/guides/adapter-vs-converter says 'A compact travel converter is usually an electronic voltage reducer designed for short sessions', that 'manufacturer manuals commonly exclude electronics outright', and that a converter 'does not resolve unknown frequency'. globalplugs.com/blog/voltage-converter-vs-adapter says combo adapter-converter products are 'rated for very low wattage (typically 25-100 W) and provide unstable voltage' and that 'transformer-based converters are usually more reliable for heating appliances'. voltwander.com/faq only says a converter is 'also called a transformer' and gives regional frequencies. So the general idea that the converter type limits which devices work is already partly covered. None of them says that one combo unit has some sockets that convert and some that pass the wall voltage straight through, or names what a specific product is approved for. ChatGPT's own answer showed Ceptics 200 W and TESSAN 250 W without either point. travelpowerpro.com (TLS error) and the digitalcameraworld Ceptics review (body truncated) could not be read.
decides: Yes, such products exist, but the mechanism means the answer has to say which kind. The TESSAN TC03 is a 250 W step-down unit that TESSAN pitches for phones, tablets, cameras, headphones and small electronics. Those devices are almost always 100–240 V already and only need the plug adapter, so it fits only the few 110V-only small electronics. Shoppers wanting a 110V-only hair dryer or straightener are steered by TESSAN to its 2000 W combo's converter section. Even then, only that section steps down; its other sockets give 220–240 V. This keeps the TC03 as the pick for small 110V-only electronics, and the page should carry a socket warning for any combo unit.
